analysis.title: Conviction Collapse: Hedge Fund Leverage Hits "Liberation Day" Lows As Everything But The VIX Screams Fear
key_insights: Goldman PB: US fundamental L/S net leverage fell a third straight week, down 2.2 points to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and in the 2nd percentile over five years. The long/short ratio fell 1.9% to 1.57 (1st percentile over five years, 0th percentile over one year). Net leverage is down 8.5 points year to date.
Gross leverage is little changed at 209.2% versus about 210% a week earlier, in the 79th percentile over five years. Funds are keeping the book large but making it more market-neutral.

Goldman's Monetary Policy Optimism factor fell to about -8 (last print -7.98), versus an all-time low of -9.38 in a series back to 1991. Only the 2020 Covid crash and the 2022 hiking shock were meaningfully lower.

Goldman's Cullen Morgan sees a trade in a Fed narrative snapback: Real Estate, Utilities, Russell and Homebuilders have the highest beta to the Monetary Policy factor relative to their implied vol levels. BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky also flagged XLU as a tactical bounce candidate.

CFTC data through Sep 29: non-dealers sold S&P 500 futures in five of the last six weeks, $68B in total. Morgan calls it one of the most aggressive bouts of selling on record. Only the 2020 and 2022 liquidations were larger, and the record six-week outflow is -$83.5B.
Goldman's US Sentiment Indicator has posted a fifth consecutive negative reading at -0.74, after -0.9 the prior week (the lowest since August 2025).
Goldman's US Vol Panic Index is still below 2/10 (1.82). The VVIX to HYG implied vol ratio has fallen to 6.74, a 3+ year low, so implied vol stress sits in credit rather than equities.
Morgan says the market is not expecting a dramatic spillover to equities from credit and rates stress, and that VIX upside convexity remains extremely attractive for those who disagree.

JPMorgan credit strategist Saul Doctor's Fear & Greed index hit 83 last week, above the 80 trigger, which he reads as a contrarian buy signal on credit after a widening he attributes to higher rates and rates volatility.

Goldman PB: US Tech was the only sector net bought in September, the largest percentage buying since February 2025. Cyclicals, defensives and consumer discretionary were net sold. The US Info Tech L/S ratio is only in the 25th percentile over five years.

Morgan calls Iran one of, if not the largest, overhang in the market. Goldman's Vickie Chang maps Nasdaq 100 at +7.5% in an oil relief scenario versus -4.8% on escalation, with oil down 28% and 10Y Treasuries rallying 33bp in the relief case.

Goldman's desk saw meaningful QQQ upside bought in the latter half of last week. Morgan prefers outright calls out to November. JPMorgan's Andrew Tyler flipped to Tactically Bullish on Sep 28 and says a US/Iran deal would be the biggest catalyst and would squeeze EU and RTY higher. JPM also notes President Trump has said the bombing is likely to resume after the midterms.

Consensus expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y, the highest heading into a reporting season since 2021, down from Q2 growth of 51% headline and 33% excluding other income from equity stakes. Goldman expects above-consensus results. JPMorgan's ~29% estimate may prove light. The top 10 contributors are expected to account for over two-thirds of aggregate S&P 500 EPS growth.

Morgan's summary: equity fundamentals are intact but challenged by a difficult macro environment. Dovish Fed speak and a weaker-than-expected jobs report should calm factor vol and let indices reach escape velocity through earnings. QQQ upside into earnings looks too low.
The S&P 500 is less than 1% from its highs and the Nasdaq is at new highs, while positioning is near five-year lows and sentiment is weak. Friday's payrolls print was 29K, below all estimates.
